data.name: Erik
data.gender_notes: Erik is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The Old Norse name Erik was derived from the Old Norse word erikr, which meant 'ruler', 'king' or 'master'. In Christian tradition, it is associated with the biblical figure Erik the Red who is believed to have discovered Greenland in the late 9th or early 10th century AD. Erik's name is also linked to the Old Testament character Ezekiel, meaning 'God strengthens' or 'God will strengthen', which adds a spiritual dimension to the name's meaning.
data.etymology: Erik belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rule, ruler, master.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Erik total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: אריק
in_hebrew.meaning: משמעות השם אריק היא שליט נצחי או שליט עולם
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אריק נגזר מהשורש העברי 'אריק' שפירושו שליט או מלך. הוא קשור למושג שליטה וריבונות, ומשמש כסמל לשליטה נצחית או עולמית. השם אריק מופיע בתרבויות שונות ומשויך לאיכויות של מנהיגות וכוח.

in_greek.name: Ερίκ
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Ερίκ σημαίνει αιώνιος κυβερνήτης ή παγκόσμιος κυρίαρχος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ερίκ έχει τις ρίζες του στην ελληνική και εβραϊκή γλώσσα. Προέρχεται από τον όρο 'אריק' (Erik) που σημαίνει 'αιώνιος κυβερνήτης' ή 'παγκόσμιος κυρίαρχος'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοιοι όροι χρησιμοποιούνται για να περιγράψουν τον Ιησού Χριστό ως τον Βασιλιά των Βασιλέων και τον Κύριο των Κυρίων. Το όνομα Ερίκ αντανακλά έννοιες όπως η αιωνιότητα, η δύναμη και η ηγεσία.

in_latin.name: Erik
in_latin.meaning: The name Erik means eternal ruler or ever-powerful
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Erik is derived from the Old Norse term 'Eiríkr', which means 'eternal ruler' or 'ever-powerful'. This name was popularized in Europe through the Viking Age and was associated with several saints and monarchs. In Christian tradition, Erik symbolizes strength, leadership, and eternal dominion.

in_english.name: Erik
in_english.meaning: Erik means eternal ruler or powerful leader in Christian tradition
in_english.long_meaning: The name Erik originates from the Old Norse 'Eiríkr', meaning 'eternal ruler' or 'ever-powerful'. It has been adopted into various cultures and is associated with Christian saints and monarchs. Erik symbolizes leadership, strength, and eternal dominion, reflecting its roots in both Norse and biblical traditions.

data.cultural_impact: Erik is a Scandinavian name with Norse roots that conjures images of brave, ruled kings, conquering Nordic explorers and fearless warriors. It is a name that carries the rich history and heritage of the North European cultures.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Erik has its roots in the Old Norse word erikr, which translates to 'ruler' or 'king'. Additionally, the Old Testament etymology of the name Ezekiel translates to 'God strengthens', which adds a deeper layer of spiritual meaning to the name Erik. This name represents not only the earthly power and authority of a well-respected leader, but also the divine grace and support from God to carry on important missions and challenges. The name Erik can be seen as a reflection of not only humanity's strength, but also God's divine presence and assistance.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Erik is of Old Norse origin, derived from Eirikr, meaning "ruler of all" or "ever ruler." In Christian context, it symbolizes leadership grounded in faith and strength in the Lord. Erik embodies the spiritual warrior, leading others to the light and ruling with compassion and wisdom.

biblical_reference.note: The name Erik does not appear directly in the Bible but is related to terms used to describe God's sovereignty.

historical_references.reference: Erik the Red was a Norse chieftain who is best known for discovering Greenland in the late 10th century.
